The shaft is a solid circular bar of diameter d = 30 mm and total length L = 1200 mm, fixed at x = 0 and free at x = 1200 mm.
The material is AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76923.1 MPa.
The cross-section is solid circular throughout; the polar moment of inertia is J = π d⁴ / 32 and the outer radius is c = d / 2 = 15 mm.
Two concentrated torques are applied: T2 = −200 000 N·mm at x = 400 mm and T1 = +200 000 N·mm at x = 1200 mm.
The shaft is in static equilibrium; verify that the reaction torque at the fixed end x = 0 is zero because T1 + T2 = 0.
The shaft is divided into two segments: Segment 1 from x = 0 to x = 400 mm, and Segment 2 from x = 400 mm to x = 1200 mm.
Determine the constant internal torque in each segment by cutting the shaft and summing external torques on one side of the cut.
Compute the maximum torsional shear stress in each segment using τ_max = T_int · c / J.
Compute the angle of twist of each segment using φ_seg = T_int · L_seg / (G · J), then sum to obtain the total angle of twist at the free end x = 1200 mm.
State the assumptions explicitly: small-deformation linear-elastic behavior, purely torsional loading with no transverse force, axial force, or bending, uniform solid circular cross-section, and torques applied about the shaft axis with no warping restraint at the fixed end.
Present the governing relations (equilibrium, τ = T r / J, φ = T L / (G J)) before substituting numerical values.
Report all results with appropriate units (N·mm or N·m for torque, MPa for stress, radians and degrees for angle of twist).
